newsitem.title: UK: EU 48-hour week rule to cost UK 4,500 jobs - report.
newsitem.headline: EU 48-hour week rule to cost UK 4,500 jobs - report.

text.p: The European Court ruling this week forcing the UK to abide by the European Union's 48-hour working week regulation will cost the British economy 4,500 jobs, according to a report published on Monday.

The Centre for Economics and Business Research (CEBR) estimated the directive would immediately reduce productivity by 0.1 percent per week, then reduce it again by another 0.2 percent due to time spent on increased record keeping.
"(There will also) possibly be some upward impact on the overtime component of wages from the improved negotiating power of workers' representatives," the report said.
Adding this up, CEBR estimates a total addition of 0.5 percent on unit costs, or 2.5 billion stg, which it equates to the loss of 4,500 jobs.
The report said the directive could also add 0.1 percent to inflation the year after it is introduced.
